result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers separate the annual default from the hard-to-read monthly price, and both get the numbers right ($7.50/mo, $65.89 saved, about 42%). B gives a firmer recommendation and explains the risks more fully: trust, refunds, chargebacks, bad reviews and churn at renewal. It also proposes an A/B test that tracks refund rate and 90-day retention as well as sign-ups. A opens with 'Partly' but then advises against pre-selecting while still accepting it with conditions, which makes its recommendation less clear. A also says 'you'll get most of the lift' without support. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers give a clear recommendation, separate pre-selecting annual from burying the monthly price, and get the math right ($7.50/mo, $65.89 saved, about 42%). A wins because it names the specific risks of the grey text (refunds, chargebacks, bad reviews, faster churn at renewal) and proposes a test that tracks conversion, refund rate and 90-day retention. B has the better concrete plan-card mockup, but it only tracks 30-day refunds and cancellations, and its claim 'you'll get most of the lift' is unsupported.
